value.event: At the Shitou affair the six armies routed; soldiers plundered the capital, reaching both palaces.
Wang Dun's Shitou incident let troops loot the capital.

changedUnits.zh: 及石頭之事，六軍大潰，兵人抄掠京邑，爰及二宮。
changedUnits.en: Wang Dun's Shitou disaster let troops sack both palace compounds.
changedUnits.literal: At the Shitou affair the six armies routed; soldiers plundered the capital, reaching both palaces.

nearby.zh: 是年三月，王敦有石頭之變，二宮陵辱，大臣誅死，僭逾無上，故旱尤甚也。
nearby.en: Wang Dun's Shitou mutiny, double-palace outrage, and ministerial bloodshed deepened the drought.
nearby.literal: That year's third month Wang Dun staged the Shitou coup; both palaces were humiliated; great ministers were executed; presumption beyond the throne — therefore the drought was especially severe.

nearby.zh: 建興中，江南謠歌曰：訇如白坑破，合集持作甒。
nearby.en: Wu dialect song opened with the white-pit couplet.
nearby.literal: Mid-Jianxing a Jiangnan ballad ran: "Boom — white pit breaks; gather shards to make a jar.

nearby.zh: 揚州破換敗，吳興覆瓿甊。」
nearby.en: Yangzhou smashes and falls; Wuxing overturns pots and urns."
nearby.literal: Yangzhou smashes and falls; Wuxing overturns pots and urns."

nearby.en: Commentary: white again signaled Jin metal.

nearby.zh: 坑器有口屬甕，瓦甕質剛，亦金之類也。
nearby.en: Pottery counted as hard "metal" in the correlative scheme.
nearby.literal: Pit vessels have mouths like urns; earthen urns are hard — also a kind of metal.

nearby.zh: 「訇如白坑破」者，言二都傾覆，王室大壞也。
nearby.en: "Boom — white pit breaks" means both capitals fell and the royal house shattered.
nearby.literal: "Boom — white pit breaks" means both capitals fell and the royal house shattered.

nearby.zh: 「合集持作甒」者，元帝鳩集遺餘，以主社稷，未能克復中原，但偏王江南，故其喻也。
nearby.en: "Gather shards to make a jar" means Yuan-di rounded up survivors to sustain the altars, could not reconquer the north, only ruled south of the river — hence the metaphor.
nearby.literal: "Gather shards to make a jar" means Yuan-di rounded up survivors to sustain the altars, could not reconquer the north, only ruled south of the river — hence the metaphor.

nearby.zh: 及石頭之事，六軍大潰，兵人抄掠京邑，爰及二宮。
nearby.en: Wang Dun's Shitou disaster let troops sack both palace compounds.
nearby.literal: At the Shitou affair the six armies routed; soldiers plundered the capital, reaching both palaces.

nearby.zh: 其後三年，錢鳳復攻京邑，阻水而守，相持月餘日，焚燒城邑，井堙木刊矣。
nearby.en: Qian Feng's second siege charred Jiankang and ruined its wells and groves.
nearby.literal: Three years later Qian Feng again attacked the capital, blocked the river and held, faced off over a month, burned towns, filled wells and felled trees.

nearby.zh: 鳳等敗退，沈充將其党還吳興，官軍踵之，蹈藉郡縣，充父子授首，黨與誅者以百數。
nearby.en: Shen Chong's retreat ended in beheadings and mass executions.
nearby.literal: When Feng retreated, Shen Chong led his party back to Wuxing; imperial troops followed, trampling commanderies; Chong and son lost their heads; over a hundred accomplices were executed.

nearby.zh: 所謂「揚州破換敗，吳興覆瓿甊」，瓿甊瓦器，又小於甒也。
nearby.en: This is the so-called "Yangzhou smashes — Wuxing overturns pots"; pots are earthenware smaller than jars.
nearby.literal: This is the so-called "Yangzhou smashes — Wuxing overturns pots"; pots are earthenware smaller than jars.

nearby.zh: 明帝太甯初，童謠曰：「惻惻力力，放馬山側。
nearby.en: Early Emperor Ming's Taining years a rhyme said: "Sighing, straining — loose horses on the hillside.
nearby.literal: Early Emperor Ming's Taining years a rhyme said: "Sighing, straining — loose horses on the hillside.

nearby.en: Great horse dies, small horse starves.
nearby.literal: Great horse dies, small horse starves.

nearby.en: High mountain collapses; stones break themselves."
nearby.literal: High mountain collapses; stones break themselves."
